1.explanation:
All of the layout problems stem from CSS in StyledCalendar.js. In particular: 
• StyledWeek uses “flex-justify: between” which is not a valid, cross-browser CSS property. Modern browsers ignore it gracefully, but IE11 never applies any justification, collapsing all day cells into one column. It should use “justify-content: space-between” instead.  
• StyledWeeksContainer and StyledDay rely on dimensions and flex properties that IE11 supports only when the standard unprefixed CSS properties are used. Ensuring proper flexbox syntax (e.g. display: flex; flex-direction: row; justify-content: space-between) and adding any necessary -ms- prefix or fallback will restore the grid layout in IE11.  
Because the issue is purely in how the weeks and day cells are styled, fixing those styled‐component definitions will resolve the broken calendar display in IE11.
1.bug_scenario: When viewed in IE11, the Grommet Calendar’s grid collapses into a single column: the days of the month stack vertically and many of the numbers do not render correctly. The flex layout that normally arranges dates in rows of weeks is not applied in IE11.

2.explanation: The Calendar relies entirely on styled-components in StyledCalendar.js to build its grid via CSS flex.  StyledWeek uses a nonstandard ‘flex-justify’ shorthand that IE11 doesn’t recognize (it needs ‘justify-content: space-between’) and StyledDayContainer declares ‘flex: 0 0’ (a two-value shorthand IE11 treats as invalid).  As a result, IE11 ignores the flex layout rules and stacks every cell in one column.  Updating StyledWeek to use the standard justify-content property and giving StyledDayContainer a valid three-value flex shorthand (e.g. flex: 0 0 auto) restores the seven-column layout in IE11.
2.bug_scenario: When opening the Grommet v2 Calendar in IE11, the month grid no longer lays out in seven columns.  Instead, each day cell collapses into a single vertical stack beneath the header (you can see date numbers 8, 15, 22, 29 running down in one column).  The header text ("July 2018") still renders, but the grid itself is broken.
